entry.title: Sang-Jun receives the Best Paper Award at KCC2026!

link.title: Sang-Jun receives the Best Paper Award at KCC2026!

entry.content:
We are pleased to announce that Sang-Jun Park, an undergraduate intern at SATA Lab, has received the Best Paper Award in the Undergraduate/Junior Paper Competition at the 2026 Korea Computer Congress (KCC 2026), organized by the Korean Institute of Information Scientists and Engineers.

His award-winning paper, “Runtime Rule Lifecycle Management Framework for 100GbE FPGA-Based Network Packet Inspection Systems,” presents an FPGA-based framework that treats packet-inspection rules as runtime data, enabling rule installation, activation, query, update, deactivation, and rollback without FPGA resynthesis or partial reconfiguration. Its on-chip double-bank rule store allows a new rule version to be validated and activated atomically while the current rule version continues to serve the packet-inspection datapath.

The prototype was implemented on an AMD/Xilinx Alveo U50 and configured to support 64K normalized rules. It achieves an FPGA-side image-loading time of 11.4 ms and an atomic rule-activation latency of approximately 15 μs, while the management logic consumes only 1.18% of LUTs and 0.83% of registers.

We are extremely proud of Sang-Jun’s dedication, persistence, and growth throughout this research. As his advisor, it is especially rewarding to see his efforts recognized through this achievement.

Congratulations, Sang-Jun! We look forward to his continued contributions and future accomplishments in the field of network systems architecture.

entry.title: SATA Lab released blueYosys, a boilerplate codebase for embedded FPGA kernel development via YosysHQ & BSV!

link.title: SATA Lab released blueYosys, a boilerplate codebase for embedded FPGA kernel development via YosysHQ & BSV!

entry.content:
After releasing blueVitis, I’m excited to share our second open-source FPGA development project: blueYosys.

blueYosys is an Advanced, High-Performance Boilerplate Codebase for Lattice ECP5-Based Embedded FPGA Kernel Development using the Yosys Open-Source Toolchain and Bluespec SystemVerilog (BSV).

It provides a transparent end-to-end development flow: Bluespec Compiler → Yosys → nextpnr → ecppack

With blueYosys, users can develop BSV hardware kernels, run Bluesim simulations, generate synthesizable Verilog, perform synthesis and place-and-route, create FPGA bitstreams, program the board, and inspect timing and resource-utilization reports through a consistent Makefile-based workflow.

Our goal is to help students, researchers, and FPGA developers spend less time rebuilding board and toolchain infrastructure and more time exploring hardware architecture, data movement, pipelining, parallelism, timing, and resource trade-offs.

If you’re building embedded FPGA applications in BSV and want a reusable development environment instead of wiring the full workflow from scratch, we’d love for you to check out blueYosys and share feedback!

Please check and explore our blueYosys here, blueYosys 😄

entry.title: Our paper has been accepted to ICCAD!

link.title: Our paper has been accepted to ICCAD!

entry.content:
We’re excited to share that one of our works, “FMiner: CPU-FPGA Heterogeneous Framework for Frequent Itemset Mining and Beyond,” has been accepted to the ‘IEEE/ACM International Conference on Computer-Aided Design (ICCAD)’!

Once again, our group proves that CPU-FPGA heterogeneous computing platforms have become a gold standard for maximizing accelerator efficacy by overcoming inherent bottlenecks and applying our novel application-driven cross-layer system architectural solutions to another new application domain: data mining.

Huge congratulations to our first author, Esmerald Aliaj at UC Irvine, and sincere thanks to my esteemed advisor, Professor Sang Woo Jun, for his invaluable guidance and support.😄

entry.title: SATA Lab released blueVitis, a boilerplate codebase for AMD FPGA kernel development using Bluespec SystemVerilog!

link.title: SATA Lab released blueVitis, a boilerplate codebase for AMD FPGA kernel development using Bluespec SystemVerilog!

entry.content:
We’re excited to share, blueVitis, an advanced and high-performance boilerplate codebase for AMD FPGA kernel development using Bluespec SystemVerilog!

It provides a research-ready starting point for building custom FPGA accelerators, combining BSV-based hardware design, host-side C++ control, and an automated Vitis build flow into a clean and extensible framework.

With its one-touch Makefile system, blueVitis automates the path from BSV-to-Verilog compilation to Vivado IP packaging, Vitis .xclbin linking, and host C++ compilation, helping researchers focus on architectural ideas rather than repetitive integration work.

The current environment targets Ubuntu 24.04, AMD Vitis 2025.02, XRT, and BSC, and the repository includes multiple working examples using HBM-connected, direct host-connected, and PLRAM-connected, tested on Alveo U50.

If you’re building AMD FPGA applications in BSV and want a reusable development environment instead of wiring the full workflow from scratch, we’d love for you to check out blueVitis and share feedback!

Please check and explore our blueVitis here, blueVitis 😄
entry.summary: We’re excited to share, blueVitis, an advanced and high-performance boilerplate codebase for AMD FPGA kernel development using Bluespec SystemVerilog!

entry.title: Our paper has been accepted to ISCA!

link.title: Our paper has been accepted to ISCA!

entry.content:
We’re excited to share that our paper, “Lembas: Cost-Efficient Genome Alignment with External Memory and FPGA Acceleration,” has been accepted to the ‘International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)’!

Lembas showcases beautiful architectural solutions for genome alignment, including FPGA time sharing, a fully external-memory-based ColumnSort, and tiled traceback.

This work is another step forward in showing that we are pioneers in architecture for bioinformatics and proving that the collaboration between ARDA Group at UC Irvine and our lab is still powerful.

Huge congratulations to our first author, Seongyoung kang at Meta, and sincere thanks to my esteemed advisor, Professor Sang Woo Jun, for their invaluable guidance and support.😄
entry.summary: We’re excited to share that our paper, “Lembas: Cost-Efficient Genome Alignment with External Memory and FPGA Acceleration,” has been accepted to the ‘International Symposium on Computer Architecture (ISCA)’!

entry.title: SATA Lab received a generous donation from AMD!

link.title: SATA Lab received a generous donation from AMD!

entry.content:
We’re grateful to AMD for the generous donation of an Xilinx Alveo U50 datacenter accelerator card to our lab!

Datacenter-class but mid-range FPGA infrastructure is essential for translating architectural ideas into real, measurable system impact, especially as modern workloads become increasingly constrained by data movement, irregularity, and end-to-end bottlenecks rather than raw compute alone. The Alveo U50 will strengthen our ability to prototype and evaluate domain-specific, system-aware acceleration across a range of applications, including network security (IPS/IDS), graph neural network, SAT solving, and large-scale genomics computing.

We’re excited to use this platform to explore new hardware–software co-designs and practical heterogeneous systems that deliver both high performance and energy efficiency at scale.

Thank you again to AMD for supporting academic research and helping advance industry–academia collaboration! 😄
entry.summary: We’re grateful to AMD for the generous donation of an Xilinx Alveo U50 datacenter accelerator card to our lab!
